subject: Usage variance and quality regression readout
messages:
From: Rachel Song <rachel.song@atrium.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-07-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: sudden uptick in tokens + drop in response quality (renewal check)

Hi Soojin / Marissa,

Quick heads-up from our end ahead of next week's renewal check: over the past 6 days our token spend is up ~28% vs. the prior two-week baseline, but we've also observed a small (4-7%) drop in classification accuracy on our critical intents. Latency is steady, but user complaints about hallucination-like responses have spiked.

I've attached a small sample set (sample_prompts.csv) and the weekly inference metrics PDF — the time window shows the jump starting 2027-07-11 after we pushed a model variant you recommended. Can your team help triage whether this is model drift vs. a prompt/attention/regression introduced by the variant?

Immediate asks:
- Can you confirm which model variant we rolled to on 2027-07-11 and whether any quantization profile changed?
- Any quick mitigations we can apply (rollback, reduce max_tokens, change routing) before our renewal meeting on 2027-07-21?
- Requesting a brief ops+product sync tomorrow if possible — we're tight on timeline.

Thanks,
Rachel
Product Ops | Atrium Labs
Attachments: sample_prompts.csv (csv), inference_metrics_weekly.pdf (pdf)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Song <rachel.song@atrium.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-07-17T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: sudden uptick in tokens + drop in response quality (renewal check)

Hi Rachel — thanks for the data and the heads-up. I pulled the attachment and started a quick pass on the metrics.

Short answers up-front:
- Model variant: we promoted rwd-7b-v2-int8 on 2027-07-11 for the route you use. No change to global quantization profiles, but we did enable an alternative attention kernel optimized for long prefix caching on that variant.
- Quick mitigations we can try today: pin the route to rwd-7b-v1 (previous stable), cap max_tokens to 256 for the affected route, and temporarily disable the long-prefix attention kernel (falls back to the prior kernel).

I've attached an initial checklist I recommend we follow for triage (initial-checklist.xlsx). Proposed immediate plan:
1) I can toggle the route pin to v1 for a 2-hour canary to measure metric rollback.
2) karthik will run a short KV-cache/attention regression test to confirm if the kernel change explains the accuracy delta.
3) If the canary shows improvement, we schedule a controlled roll-forward with a tuned prompt shim to reduce token burn.

Are you available for a 30m sync today at 11:30 PT? If not, we can do 14:00 PT.

— Soojin
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
Attachments: initial-checklist.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Song <rachel.song@atrium.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-07-17T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: sudden uptick in tokens + drop in response quality (renewal check)

Quick technical readout from our side after an initial log sweep:
- The rwd-7b-v2-int8 rollout included a new attention kernel that improves throughput for long-context streaming, but in some prompt shapes it slightly alters tokenization boundaries (we saw token_count +12-18% on multi-turn prompts in your sample). That explains token burn.
- The quality regression appears correlated with a subtle change in top-p/token sampling defaults baked into v2's generation config. Not a model weight drift — more config/decoding behavior.

Immediate options:
A) Roll back to rwd-7b-v1 for affected routes (fastest, minimal customer impact) — we should expect token spend to return to baseline within minutes.
B) Keep v2 but override generation config for the route (lower top_p, slightly higher temperature control) — this needs a 1-2 hour test window.
C) Keep v2 and apply a prompt normalization shim to reduce multi-turn token duplication (medium effort).

Operational notes: enabling/disabling the attention kernel is a config flip (no deploy). We're ready to run A as a canary; I'll also prepare a short ops playbook with rollback steps and monitoring thresholds.

Proposing: run canary rollback (A) for 2 hours while we test B in parallel. If rollback restores accuracy and lowers tokens, we discuss controlled roll-forward with B as the tuning path.

I'll upload the ops playbook and monitoring dashboard links to the drive after the call.

-karthik
Senior Technical Program Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: ops_playbook.md

Subject: Action items and call scheduled — renewal prep

Rachel — thanks again for flagging this. Recap of what we'll do before the renewal review on 2027-07-21: 

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Soojin: schedule 11:30 PT triage call (today) and execute 2-hour canary rollback to rwd-7b-v1 for the affected route (start immediately after call).
- Karthik: run config/decoding A/B in parallel (option B) and deliver a short ops_playbook.md + monitoring thresholds by EOD.
- Marissa: prepare a short ROI slide that compares token spend delta vs. cost savings if we throttle top_p and cap tokens (for renewal decision pack).

If the canary restores accuracy and reduces token spend we will: 1) keep the route pinned to v1, 2) schedule a controlled roll-forward with tuned generation config, and 3) update the renewal ask to include a short pilot (2 weeks) to validate tuned v2 before committing to long-term capacity changes.

Call invite: 2027-07-17T11:30:00-07:00 (30m) — link in drive. Please confirm you can make it.

Best,
Soojin Lee
